intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen (COL9A2; 120260) on chromosome 1p34.2.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia-2 (EDM2) is caused by mutation in the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region.
checks.explanation: The paper identifies a COL9A2 mutation in a family with EDM2 and links COL9A2 exon 3 skipping mutations to EDM2.

checks.claim: COL9A2 encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to COL9A2 as the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX.

checks.claim: The COL9A2 gene is located on chromosome 1p34.2.
checks.evidence_quote: novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state the chromosomal location. It counts as supported only because a standard gene location in the draft is treated as restating the paper.

paragraphs.text: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia with mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis (Briggs et al. (1994)). Fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses are characteristic (Versteylen et al. (1988)). Pain and stiffness of the knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints begin in childhood, and affected individuals are prone to early degenerative joint disease (Fiedler et al. (2002)). In EDM2, the hips are not markedly affected at an early age (Fiedler et al. (2002)).

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is associated with mild short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is associated with early-onset osteoarthrosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses are characteristic of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: It is suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses as characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia, in the context of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

checks.claim: In multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, pain and stiffness of the knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints begin in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Beginning in childhood, the disease leads to pain and stiffness of knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints.
checks.explanation: The paper describes this in one family with the EDM2 variant of MED, not in MED in general.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia are prone to early degenerative joint disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Finally, affected individuals are prone to the development of early degenerative joint disease.
checks.explanation: The paper says this about affected members of the EDM2 family, not about MED in general.

checks.claim: In EDM2, the hips are not markedly affected at an early age.
checks.evidence_quote: a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with MED. Linkage studies with chromosome 19 markers excluded the previously identified chromosome 19 interval (EDM1) in this family. Using this family, they identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing COL9A2, the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
checks.explanation: The study used a large MED family.

checks.claim: In the large MED family studied by Briggs et al. (1994), linkage studies with chromosome 19 markers excluded the previously identified chromosome 19 MED interval (EDM1).
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
checks.explanation: The previously linked interval was excluded. Calling it EDM1 is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: Using the large MED family, Briggs et al. (1994) identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1.
checks.evidence_quote: Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: The chromosome 1p MED locus identified by Briggs et al. (1994) lies in a region containing COL9A2, the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: in a region containing the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Warman et al. (1994) used fluorescence in situ hybridization to map the COL9A2 gene to chromosome 1p32.3-p33.

checks.claim: Warman et al. (1994) used fluorescence in situ hybridization to map the COL9A2 gene to chromosome 1p32.3-p33.
checks.evidence_quote: COL9A2 was mapped to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 using fluorescence in situ hybridization.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the FISH mapping of COL9A2 to 1p32.3-p33 directly.

paragraphs.text: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is genetically heterogeneous. A form of MED had been linked to chromosome 19, but Briggs et al. (1994) excluded that interval in their family and identified a second MED locus on chromosome 1p. Nakashima et al. (2005) discussed MED associated with mutation in the DTDST (SLC26A2) gene.

checks.claim: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19
checks.explanation: Heterogeneity follows directly: one form of MED maps to chromosome 19, while this family's MED excludes chromosome 19 and maps to chromosome 1p.

checks.claim: A form of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia had been linked to chromosome 19 before Briggs et al. (1994).
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19
checks.explanation: Stated directly as earlier work.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) excluded the chromosome 19 MED interval in their family.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Briggs et al. (1994) identified a second MED locus on chromosome 1p.
checks.evidence_quote: Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1
checks.explanation: This is a second locus, distinct from the chromosome 19 interval. The title calls it EDM2.

checks.claim: Nakashima et al. (2005) discussed multiple epiphyseal dysplasia associated with mutation in the DTDST (SLC26A2) gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
checks.explanation: The title alone shows that the paper discusses MED in relation to DTDST mutation, which is enough for this broad claim.

paragraphs.text: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).

checks.claim: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in the COL9A2 gene causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
checks.evidence_quote: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
checks.explanation: The claim matches what the title says.

checks.claim: COL9A2 encodes the alpha-2 chain of collagen IX, a fibril-associated collagen.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2
checks.explanation: The title calls collagen IX fibril-associated and says COL9A2 encodes its alpha-2 chain.

paragraphs.text: In a family with MED, Fiedler et al. (2002) screened candidate regions for mutations. They found a novel G-to-C point mutation at position -1 in the exon 3/intron 3 splicing region of the COL9A2 gene, which they thought most probably alters splicing. Taking their results together with previous reports, Fiedler et al. (2002) concluded that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen may be relatively common in patients with EDM2, a subtype of MED in which the hips are not markedly affected at an early age.

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) screened candidate regions for mutations in a family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation
checks.explanation: The family has a variant of MED, and the authors screened candidate regions.

checks.claim: In a family with MED, Fiedler et al. (2002) found a novel G-to-C point mutation at position -1 in the exon 3/intron 3 splicing region of the COL9A2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region. This G --> C substitution
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) thought that the G-to-C mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region most probably alters splicing.
checks.evidence_quote: This G --> C substitution most probably induces an alteration of the splicing process.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Fiedler et al. (2002) concluded that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen may be relatively common in patients with EDM2.
checks.evidence_quote: Together with previous reports our results indicate that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a special subtype
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: EDM2 is a subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia in which the hips are not markedly affected at an early age.
checks.evidence_quote: a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2)
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Hips not markedly affected at early age
